findings.title: Write path never rechecks the cache and can clear a good entry
findings.body: GetWebAssets snapshots entryPointAssetsCache under a read lock, drops that lock, then later takes the write lock and always reloads. It never re-reads entryPointAssetsCache after Lock, and it always stores the load result, including a nil result when readWebAssetsFromFile fails. Every caller that observed a cold cache therefore runs the load, and a later waiter that fails (missing manifest, transient read error, bad JSON) overwrites a cache entry an earlier waiter already published. Non-dev callers then miss the cache and hit the filesystem again. The same stampede also repeats the manifest read serially while holding the exclusive lock, so startup latency stacks instead of one successful load serving the other waiters. After acquiring the write lock, return the existing pointer when cfg.Env is not Dev and the cache is already non-nil, and do not replace a populated cache with a failed nil result.

findings.title: Process-wide exclusive lock is held across manifest I/O
findings.body: The write lock taken at the start of the slow path is held, via defer Unlock, until GetWebAssets returns, and that section calls readWebAssetsFromFile (os.Open plus JSON decode). Lock hold time is therefore disk latency, and a slow or stuck open blocks every other GetWebAssets caller in the process, not just the request that is loading. In dev the fast path is never taken (the early return requires Env != Dev), so every call takes this exclusive lock and reads the manifest under it, serializing concurrent renders. If the load fails the cache is left nil, so later requests keep queueing on the same mutex to repeat the failed open. Read the manifest outside the lock and hold entryPointAssetsCacheMu only to publish a successful result.

findings.title: Race fix has no concurrent regression test
findings.body: This change only adds a mutex around the global asset cache and does not add a test that calls GetWebAssets concurrently on a cold cache, or one where one load succeeds and another fails. The missing re-check under the write lock and the nil overwrite of entryPointAssetsCache would not be caught, and the original data race can regress. A race-detector test with several goroutines, including a failing manifest read, should assert that a successful non-dev result stays cached and is what the other callers receive.
